candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the request URL: the active page name, the nested component id and the event type are parsed from the path (e.g. /index.runGC:action), and the containing page name is supplied via the query parameter t:cp (value < whitelist-only page name>). No authentication or whitelist membership is required. With the default WhitelistAnalyzer (LocalhostOnly), a remote client is not on the whitelist, so any page annotated @WhitelistAccessOnly is normally unreachable.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched all uses of MetaDataConstants.WHITELIST_ONLY_PAGE / isWhitelistOnlyAndNotValid: the only enforcement points are the active-page check in validateAndConstructComponentEventRequest and the page-name check in checkIfPage (page render path, :483-509). The ComponentEventRequestHandler pipeline filters (ajax/TapestryModule.java:2204-2222) only enforce HTTPS redirect via the active page; ProductionModeUnknownComponentFilter and RequestOperationTracker merely resolve/log the containing page; RequestPageCacheImpl.get (:78-107) canonicalizes and loads any page without access control; canonicalizePageName accepts any registered page, including whitelist-only ones. No other validation of t:cp was found. .tml templates and test sources are not part of the visible snapshot, so a template-level or test-level mitigation could not be observed; the flaw was not executed or reproduced at runtime.
candidates.impact: Bypass of the @WhitelistAccessOnly guarantee documented as 'behave as if the page does not exist at all' for non-whitelisted clients. A remote attacker can invoke state-changing event handlers on whitelist-only pages. With the built-in pages this includes forcing a full page/class reload (onActionFromClearCaches -> ReloadHelper.forceReload), force-loading every defined page (onActionFromForceLoad, resource exhaustion) and forcing a full garbage collection (onActionFromRunGC, trivial DoS); application pages marked @WhitelistAccessOnly may expose far more sensitive administrative handlers. The same root cause also means the @Secure HTTPS-redirect check (RequestSecurityManagerImpl.checkForInsecureComponentEventRequest, invoked from TapestryModule.contributeComponentEventRequestHandler) considers only the active page, so events can be driven against secure pages over plain HTTP.
candidates.prerequisites: At least one page annotated @WhitelistAccessOnly exists (built into 5.4: PageCatalog, ServiceStatus, T5Dashboard, ComponentLibraries; also common in applications/admin libraries); the caller is not on the whitelist (default: not localhost); the caller knows one valid non-whitelist page name whose activation does not abort (e.g. index) and a component id / event on the target page (built-in PageCatalog exposes component ids runGC, forceLoad, clearCaches with the action event; for the 'action' event on such a link the event bubbles from the link component to the page's onActionFromX handler).
candidates.root_cause: ComponentEventLinkEncoderImpl.validateAndConstructComponentEventRequest() applies the whitelist check (isWhitelistOnlyAndNotValid) only to the active page decoded from the URL path. The containing page name, taken from the user-controlled query parameter t:cp (InternalConstants.CONTAINER_PAGE_NAME), is only canonicalized - never checked against MetaDataConstants.WHITELIST_ONLY_PAGE. ComponentEventRequestHandlerImpl (and AjaxComponentEventRequestHandler) then look up that containing page and dispatch the event to a component on it, so an event handler on a whitelist-only page is reached even though the whitelist check on the active page passed.
candidates.title: Whitelist-only page protection bypass via attacker-controlled t:cp (containing page) parameter
candidates.trace: decodeComponentEventRequest (ComponentEventLinkEncoderImpl:255-348) -> validateAndConstructComponentEventRequest (:350-375): isWhitelistOnlyAndNotValid(activePageName) at :359-362, then containingPageName = canonicalizePageName(request.getParameter("t:cp")) at :364-368 with no whitelist check -> new ComponentEventRequestParameters(activePageName, containingPageName, nestedComponentId, eventType, ...) -> ComponentEventRequestHandlerImpl.handle (:54-97) or AjaxComponentEventRequestHandler.handle (:68-114) -> RequestPageCache.get(containingPageName) (no access control) -> getComponentElementByNestedId(nestedComponentId) -> triggerContextEvent(eventType, ...) -> event bubbles to the whitelist-only page's handler (e.g. PageCatalog.onActionFromRunGC / onActionFromClearCaches / onActionFromForceLoad at PageCatalog.java:195-288).
candidates.unverified: No runtime confirmation was performed. Exploitability depends on the application having whitelist-only pages whose component ids/event handlers the attacker can determine (for the built-in PageCatalog these ids are fixed: runGC, forceLoad, clearCaches). It could not be verified whether a later/other configuration or an application-contributed WhitelistAnalyzer mitigates the issue, and I could not diff against the fixed upstream revision to confirm this is the exact historical CVE.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper Access Control / Authorization Bypass (CWE-284, CWE-863)

coverage_summary: Visible scope: 2,070 files (main sources of beanmodel, commons, plastic, tapestry-core, -hibernate, -ioc, -jcache, -jpa, -json, -kaptcha, -mongodb, -spring, -upload, -webresources, runner/test helpers, quickstart). Heavy focus on tapestry-core request handling and security: ComponentEventLinkEncoderImpl, ComponentEventRequestHandlerImpl, AjaxComponentEventRequestHandler, RequestSecurityManagerImpl, ClientWhitelistImpl/LocalhostOnly, whitelist meta extraction in TapestryModule, page-render/component-event decoding, RequestPageCacheImpl/PageImpl dispatch, ContextAsset/ClasspathAsset/StackAsset handlers, ResourceStreamerImpl, ContextResource/AbstractResource path handling, ClientDataEncoder/ClientDataSink/ClientPersistentFieldStorage/Form deserialization, MarkupWriter/dom escaping, ExceptionReport/ExceptionReporter, cookies, localization, and the corelib pages/components. Note: the exposed snapshot contains no .tml templates and no src/test sources, so template escaping, client-side JS behavior, and test expectations were outside the visible scope; no code was executed and no external data was consulted.
limitations: No runtime execution/tests; the candidate is a source-level lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
Templates (.tml), test sources and other non-exposed artifacts are outside the visible file set, so a mitigating template/filter or a fix-specific test could not be inspected.

Exploitability depends on application page names/component ids and whitelist analyzer configuration; only built-in whitelist-only pages (PageCatalog etc.) were verified to carry actionable event handlers.
Could not compare against upstream/fixed revisions or CVE data (not permitted), so the mapping to a specific historical CVE is inferred from code behavior, not verified.
Review was security-focused rather than exhaustive per file; lower-risk modules (mongodb, jpa, spring, json parser internals, webresources transformers) were only spot-checked.

rejected_leads.lead: ClientDataEncoderImpl falls back to the (guessable) application package name as HMAC key when tapestry.hmac-passphrase is unset, while ClientPersistentFieldStorageImpl and Form deserialize the HMAC-protected t:state:client / t:formdata data with java.io.ObjectInputStream (potential RCE via forged serialized payloads).
rejected_leads.reason: Real hardening weakness, but it is an explicitly documented and warning-logged fallback configuration choice rather than a missing check; exploitation additionally requires the symbol to be left unset and a usable gadget chain on the classpath. Selected candidate has stronger, configuration-independent source evidence of an unintended access-control flaw.

rejected_leads.lead: MavenComponentLibraryInfoSource parses pom.xml with a default DocumentBuilderFactory (no XXE hardening) at lines 57/103-104.
rejected_leads.reason: The parsed documents come from classpath META-INF/maven resources (classpath scanning), not from attacker-controlled HTTP input; no reachable untrusted XML source was found.

rejected_leads.lead: Asset request handlers (ContextAssetRequestHandler, ClasspathAssetRequestHandler, ChecksumPath) accepting arbitrary extraPath.
rejected_leads.reason: AbstractResource.forFile (tapestry-ioc AbstractResource.java:93-131) normalizes '..' and throws when escaping the root, and suffix-based protection rules block .class/.properties/.xml; no path traversal beyond the resource root was identified.

rejected_leads.lead: Cookie, redirect (DefaultRequestExceptionHandler / ResponseImpl) and module-dispatch paths.
rejected_leads.reason: Values are server-generated links or validated/encoded paths; no attacker-controlled redirect target or header injection was identified in the reviewed code.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Tapestry 5.4.4 source snapshot (2,070 visible files, main sources only). The strongest source-grounded candidate is an access-control (whitelist) bypass in the component-event request path: the containing page chosen by the user-controlled `t:cp` query parameter is never checked against the `@WhitelistAccessOnly` protection, so a non-whitelisted (e.g., remote) client can trigger event handlers on pages that are supposed to "behave as if the page does not exist at all" for such clients. Other leads (weak default HMAC passphrase for signed client data / Java deserialization, unhardened XML parsing, asset path traversal) were examined and rejected as weaker or not attacker-reachable.
